gelecek_hedef: Artemis south-polar regions (impact crater, frozen ground); Mars polar desert
baslik: Haughton Crater: K10 rover surveys and the HMP-2010 robotic convoy
nasa_ne_yapti: From 10 July to 3 August 2007, two NASA Ames K10 rovers surveyed the roughly 700 m × 700 m "Drill Hill" area inside the crater with lidar and ground-penetrating radar (CRUX GPR), with the HMP base camp acting as a lunar outpost and JSC as ground control [9]. In HMP-2010, a robotic convoy from Shackleton to Malapert was simulated with a K10 rover and the MARS-1 Humvee acting as a pressurized rover [10].

gelecek_hedef: Simple impact craters, Artemis geology training
nasa_ne_yapti: Apollo astronauts trained here from 1963 to 1970, and a tear in one astronaut's suit on the rocks led to improvements in the suit [12]. The USGS still describes the crater as an analog site [11]. An IAC-21 paper by Osinski proposes Meteor Crater, together with Mistastin, for Artemis training [30].

ad: Black Point Lava Flow, San Francisco Volcanic Field, Arizona
baslik: Black Point Lava Flow: Desert RATS pressurized rover tests
nasa_ne_yapti: In the Desert RATS tests of 2008–2012, with a landing site chosen on top of the flow, NASA simulated 3-, 14- and 28-day Lunar Electric Rover missions [14]. On the 14-day mission, a two-person crew drove the rover as far as Colton Crater and SP Crater [14]. NASA Earth Observatory reported on the late-2009 test [13].

ad: Mauna Kea, Pu'u Hiwahine (PISCES site), Hawaii
baslik: Mauna Kea: ISRU field tests of the RESOLVE prototype
nasa_ne_yapti: From 27 January to 11 February 2010, NASA ran an ISRU analog test here with CSA, DLR and NORCAT, operated by PISCES, in which KSC's RESOLVE prototype simulated prospecting for volatiles at a lunar pole [16][17]. In 2012, a robotic polar mission was simulated and RESOLVE was tested again on a CSA rover [16]. In November 2009, experiments to extract oxygen from regolith were run at the same site [18].

ad: Craters of the Moon, Idaho (Inferno Chasm)
baslik: Craters of the Moon: FINESSE volcanic mapping and ConOps tests
nasa_ne_yapti: The Ames-led FINESSE project, under SSERVI, worked here in 2014 and 2015 [19]. The team mapped volcanic landforms with LiDAR, differential GPS and drones and compared them with LRO NAC images and terrain models [19][20]. Operations concepts (ConOps) for future human–robotic exploration were also tested [20].

baslik: Kamestastin Crater: CSA-led astronaut geology training
nasa_ne_yapti: Geology training here is run by the CSA and Western University (Osinski), and NASA astronauts take part [22][30]. Kutryk (CSA) and Dominick (NASA) trained here in September 2021, and Hansen and Gibbons (CSA) with Koch and Chari (NASA) in September 2023 [22][23]. NASA's July 2024 PAC presentation lists "Fieldwork – Kamestastin" as a step in Artemis II training [24].

ad: Iceland, north of Vatnajökull National Park
gelecek_hedef: Basalt, breccia, icy ground; Artemis astronaut geology training
baslik: Iceland: Artemis II crew geology field training, 2024
nasa_ne_yapti: From 24 July to 6 August 2024, the Artemis II crew (Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen) and their backups (Douglas, Gibbons) received NASA-led field training north of Vatnajökull National Park [25][26]. They carried out daytime traverses and night traverses in low-angle light and tested sampling tools [25].

baslik: Lanzarote: ESA PANGAEA training with NASA astronauts
nasa_ne_yapti: PANGAEA is ESA's mission, not NASA's; since 2016 it has trained ESA, NASA, JAXA and Roscosmos astronauts, and one part of the programme takes place at the Ries [27]. NASA astronauts take part; NASA astronaut Jasmin Moghbeli was one of the participants of the 10th edition in 2026 [28].

NASA Ames's ARADS project, funded by PSTAR, tested a Mars-prototype drill, a sample-transfer arm and the SOLID (CAB, Spain) and WCL instruments together here [31][32]. In September 2019, the rover drove on its own to the "Playa" site and collected samples, with commands sent twice a day [32]. The site has been studied as a Mars analog since 2003 [33].

gelecek_hedef: Meridiani Planum: jarosite, hematite, Fe-S minerals
baslik: Río Tinto: MARTE robotic drilling simulation
nasa_ne_yapti: MARTE, a joint project of NASA Ames and Spain's CAB funded by ASTEP, ran from 2003 to 2005 [35]. In 2005, a one-month robotic dry-drilling mission was simulated at the edge of the open-pit mine at Peña de Hierro, and the science teams were not given prior knowledge of the site [35][37].

gelecek_hedef: Phoenix site, ground ice of northern plains
baslik: University Valley: IceBite drilling and Phoenix science tests
nasa_ne_yapti: Over three austral summers starting in 2009, the ASTEP-funded IceBite project (McKay, Ames) tested drills for reaching the ice beneath "dry permafrost" for a future Mars polar mission [40][42]. During the International Polar Year, Phoenix science questions were tested here (Tamppari et al. 2012) [41].

baslik: Svalbard: AMASE instrument tests on the FIDO rover
nasa_ne_yapti: AMASE is a Norwegian-led expedition funded by NASA ASTEP and ESA, with teams from JPL, Ames and GSFC [43]. In 2009, two instruments for MSL and four for ExoMars were tested on JPL's FIDO rover [43][44].

baslik: Lava Beds: BRAILLE cave rover mission
nasa_ne_yapti: In 2018–2019, NASA Ames's PSTAR-funded BRAILLE project ran a three-week mission here [45]. The CaveR rover was driven into Valentine Cave under a planetary mission plan, the cave was mapped with a laser scanner, and samples were taken from 9 caves [45].

ad: Pavilion Lake, British Columbia (Canada) — operations analog only, not matched
baslik: Pavilion Lake: science EVA under communication delay (operations analog)
nasa_ne_yapti: The Pavilion Lake Research Project ran from 2004 to 2015 (Lim, Ames; CSA's CARN programme) and simulated science-driven EVA with DeepWorker submersibles [47]. In 2015 (PLRP-3), EVA under communication delay was tested [47].
